If you have a bug, please [file an issue here](https://github.com/modular/modular/issues/new/choose). ## License Mojo and its contributions are licensed under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions. About Modular | MAX docs | Mojo docs | Contributing

Modular Platform

This repo hosts open-source components of the Modular Platform, a unified platform for AI development and deployment, including the MAX Framework🧑‍🚀 and the Mojo Language🔥.

Get started

Want to use MAX and Mojo in your own projects? Check out the MAX get started guide and the Mojo get started guide.

Want to experiment with functionality in MAX or Mojo? Work from the repository:

  • Run mojo on a file:

    ./bazelw run //Mojo:mojo -- Mojo/examples/hello.mojo

  • Run max to generate text with a model (requires a compatible GPU):

    ./bazelw run //max/python/max/_entrypoints:pipelines -- generate \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --max-batch-size 1 --max-length 10000 \
  --prompt "The sky is blue because"

About the repo

We're actively open-sourcing more of the Modular Platform over time.

The main components for which source is available today include:

  • Mojo compiler: /Mojo (since August 2026)
  • Mojo standard library: /Mojo/stdlib (since March 2024)
  • MAX GPU programming abstractions: /max/mojo/max/gpu (GPU programming in Mojo, since May 2025)
  • MAX accelerator library: /max/kernels (Mojo compute kernels, since May 2025)
  • MAX graph compiler: /GraphCompiler
  • MAX runtime: /MLRT
  • MAX driver: /max/driver
  • MAX AI framework: /max/python/max (model authoring in Python, since November 2025)
  • MAX model pipelines: /max/python/max/pipelines (models built on the framework, since May 2025)
  • MAX inference server: /max/python/max/serve (OpenAI-compatible endpoint, since May 2025)
  • Code examples: /max/examples and /Mojo/examples

Contribute

We accept contributions to both Mojo (Mojo contributor guide) and MAX (MAX contributor guide). For information about what changes we accept in different areas, see the Mojo contribution areas and MAX contribution areas.

We also welcome your bug reports. If you have a bug, please file an issue here.

License

Mojo and its contributions are licensed under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions. See Licenses/APACHE_LICENSE.

Portions of the MAX source code and its binary distribution are licensed under the Licenses/MAX_LICENSE, with the remainder of the source under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions. See Licenses/APACHE_LICENSE.

Third party licenses

You are entirely responsible for checking and validating the licenses of third parties (for example, Hugging Face) for related software and libraries that are downloaded.

Community & Events

There are a lot of great ways to get involved! Check out the Modular community page for details.

Thanks to our contributors

releases.name: MAX 26.7 / Mojo 1.2.0
releases.body:
In MAX 26.7, we've added Muse Glimmer and MiMo-V2.6-Flash, plus video input for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-VL. The new Decisions API returns probabilities for classification, scoring, and yes/no questions without generating text, and works with every text-generation model. Speculative decoding now applies each request's sampling settings to DFlash, DFlash2, and DSpark draft tokens, and MAX can dynamically select the verification width that delivers the best measured decode throughput. We've also made Jenga the default KV cache, added prefix caching for Qwen3.5-family and Inkling models, and enabled tiered KV connectors for recurrent-state models. Plus continued progress on the eager execution API, including your custom ops—eager execution shares a single code path with the graph compiler, so the code you run in eager mode is the same as what you compile and ship. This release also brings substantial performance improvements for models on NVIDIA B200s AMD MI355 GPUs.

releases.name: MAX 26.6 / Mojo 1.1.0
releases.body:
In MAX v26.6, we've added support for [audio generation](https://max.modular.com/serve/audio-generation/) with MiniMax-Music3, which can generate 44.1 kHz stereo music from a text prompt. We've also added support for Inkling from Thinking Machines, a multimodal model that accepts text and image inputs with NVFP4 mixture-of-experts, and GLM-5.3, plus expanded coverage across the Kimi, Qwen, and Gemma model families. Speculative decoding now supports DFlash and DSpark draft models on Gemma 4 31B, which speeds up token generation without changing the model's output. We've also sped up kernels across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, including up to 4.8× faster Gemma 4 decode attention, 7.9× faster MoE routing, 16× faster low-batch NVFP4 quantization on B200, and up to 6.6× faster decode attention projections on MI355. Plus, the [`max.gpu`](https://max.modular.com/api/mojo/max/gpu/) package now includes everything previously provided in Mojo's `std.gpu` package, making it a complete entry point for accelerator programming.

With Mojo 1.1, we've added support for inferred member references—a leading-dot form now resolves against the expected type (for example, `SIMD[.float64, 4]` instead of `SIMD[

releases.name: MAX 26.5 / Mojo 1.0.0
releases.body:
In this release, we've moved most of the GPU programming APIs out of the Mojo standard library and into a new top-level `max` package—`std.algorithm` is now `max.algorithm`, `std.benchmark` is `max.benchmark`, and `std.gpu.{compute,host,memory,sync}` is `max.gpu.*`, along with the Mojo `layout` package. All of which is now part of the new [MAX accelerator library](https://docs.modular.com/api/mojo/), which also includes the existing AI kernels. We've also extended Apple silicon GPU support back to M1 devices, and added hardware-MMA flash-attention prefill for M5 to speed up TTFT. The MAX model bring-up workflow also gains new agent skills in [our skills repo](https://github.com/modular/skills), including new `serve-model`, `benchmark-model`, `eval-model`, and `profile-model` skills. We've also expanded model coverage and capabilities, made significant strides speeding up the Python API's experimental eager interpreter, sped up various kernels across NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple GPUs, and much more to accelerate models served with MAX.

Of course, this release also brings Mojo 1.0! 🔥

releases.name: MAX 26.4 / Mojo 1.0.0b2
releases.body:
The MAX 26.4 release brings Apple silicon GPU serving to almost all compatible MAX models, with M3 and newer devices now running Llama and Qwen model families (and others that fit in system memory). We've also added support for new models, including Tencent Hunyuan Hy3-preview, LiquidAI LFM2, and GLM-5/5.1 with FP8/NVFP4 weights. DeepSeek V2 and V3 can now run on a single GPU (with block-scaled FP8 quantization for V3) and long-context sparse MLA for DeepSeek-V3.2. Gemma 4 gains native FP8 attention with an FP8 KV cache on B200 (roughly matching bf16 accuracy while doubling KV cache capacity) and NVFP4 quantization, structured output with grammar enforcement, MTP speculative decoding, and multi-GPU support for the 31B variant. MiniMax-M2 picks up MXFP4 quantization and tensor-parallel attention combined with expert-parallel MoE (TP+EP). Plus much, much more, including enhanced Prometheus metrics, improved kernel performance, new benchmark datasets, and lots of Python API upgrades.

releases.name: MAX 26.3 / Mojo 1.0.0b1
releases.body:
The Modular 26.3 release brings video generation to MAX with Wan 2.1 / 2.2 diffusion models (image-to-video and video-to-video), a new multi-GPU Python API via `max.experimental.sharding` that distributes models across a DeviceMesh with Replicated, Sharded, and Partial placement primitives, and NVFP4 grouped matmul kernels that now outperform FlashInfer on B200 for Kimi K2.5. New model support lands for Gemma 4 with multimodal vision, Qwen3 and Qwen3-VL (including MoE variants), MiniMax-M2 with 4×H100 multi-GPU serving, and FLUX.2 with TaylorSeer and TeaCache denoising caches for faster image-to-image generation.

The Mojo 1.0 beta 1 (v1.0.0b1) release introduces type refinement from compile-time assumptions: where `conforms_to(T, Trait)` clauses, `comptime if`, and `comptime assert` now narrow types automatically, eliminating the need for manual `trait_downcast` calls throughout the standard library. aiSummary.oneLiner: A unified platform for AI development and deployment, featuring the Mojo language and MAX framework.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: The Modular Platform is an integrated ecosystem designed to drastically simplify and accelerate AI development and deployment. It hosts open-source components including the MAX Framework, which optimizes and serves AI models across heterogeneous hardware, and the Mojo programming language, which combines Python's usability with C-level performance. By unifying the fragmented AI software stack, Modular allows developers to write high-performance AI applications without wrestling with complex, specialized hardware compilers. It empowers teams to build, optimize, and deploy models efficiently from a single, cohesive platform.
keyFeatures: Mojo programming language: Integrates a new language that offers Python syntax compatibility while delivering native, compiled performance.
MAX framework deployment: Provides a highly optimized inference engine to serve AI models efficiently across diverse hardware architectures.
Unified AI stack: Consolidates fragmented tools into a single platform, simplifying the pipeline from model development to production.
Hardware abstraction: Automatically optimizes code for various CPUs and GPUs without requiring developers to write hardware-specific instructions.
High-performance execution: Leverages advanced compiler technology to significantly accelerate AI workloads and tensor operations.

useCases.title: High-performance AI inference
useCases.description: Deploy complex machine learning models into production environments using the MAX framework for optimized, low-latency serving.

useCases.title: Systems-level programming
useCases.description: Utilize the Mojo language to write performance-critical components of AI applications while maintaining readable, Pythonic syntax.

useCases.title: Hardware-agnostic deployment
useCases.description: Develop AI applications once and deploy them efficiently across different hardware accelerators without rewriting the core logic.

useCases.title: Model optimization
useCases.description: Leverage the platform's advanced compiler infrastructure to automatically optimize tensor operations for maximum throughput.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: The Modular Platform is built for AI researchers, machine learning engineers, and systems developers seeking high-performance tools. It requires familiarity with Python and AI deployment architectures.
